history.fact: Debuted as the first US-market WRX in 2001.

scenes.headline: 227 Horsepower Wagon
scenes.narration: What if your grocery-getter packed 227 horsepower? Meet the Subaru Impreza WRX Wagon.

scenes.headline: Turbocharged Flat 4
scenes.narration: The 2002 WRX Wagon features a 2.0-liter turbocharged flat-four engine. It delivers 227 horsepower and 217 lb-ft of torque. With all-wheel drive and a 5-speed manual, it's ready for any adventure.

scenes.headline: WRX Debut Year
scenes.narration: In 2001, the second-gen Impreza introduced the first US-market WRX. It combined rally-inspired performance with everyday practicality.

scenes.headline: 4WD vs RSX
scenes.narration: Compare this to the Acura RSX Type-S. The Subaru's got 227 horsepower, while the RSX only has 200. But the RSX revs higher, right up to 8,000 rpm.

scenes.headline: $24K -> $20K
scenes.narration: Originally priced around $24,000, these WRX Wagons trade for about $20,000 today. With a 0 to 60 time of 5.9 seconds, it's quick for a wagon.

scenes.headline: To Daily or Not?
scenes.narration: So, would you rock a rally-bred wagon daily, or does sleek coupe styling win for you?

script: What if your grocery-getter packed 227 horsepower? Meet the Subaru Impreza WRX Wagon. The 2002 WRX Wagon features a 2.0-liter turbocharged flat-four engine. It delivers 227 horsepower and 217 lb-ft of torque. With all-wheel drive and a 5-speed manual, it's ready for any adventure. In 2001, the second-gen Impreza introduced the first US-market WRX. It combined rally-inspired performance with everyday practicality. Compare this to the Acura RSX Type-S. The Subaru's got 227 horsepower, while the RSX only has 200. But the RSX revs higher, right up to 8,000 rpm. Originally priced around $24,000, these WRX Wagons trade for about $20,000 today. With a 0 to 60 time of 5.9 seconds, it's quick for a wagon. So, would you rock a rally-bred wagon daily, or does sleek coupe styling win for you?

sections.Highlights: THIS...is a 2002 Subaru Impreza WRX Wagon, finished in Platinum Silver Metallic with a blue and gray interior. This WRX is equipped with the desirable 5-speed manual transmission, and the odometer indicates approximately 49,500 miles. The attached Carfax history report lists no accidents or odometer discrepancies in this Subaru's past. It also lists just one North Carolina owner from new. Factory equipment on this WRX includes a viscous limited-slip rear differential, a sport-tuned suspension system, cloth upholstery, a leather-wrapped MOMO steering wheel, a boost gauge, air conditioning, and a CD player. The selling dealer reports no modifications. The 2nd-generation Impreza made its debut for the 2001 model year, and it spawned the first WRX sold on the American market. Like the standard Impreza, the WRX was offered as a sedan and as a station wagon. The WRX (World Rally eXperimental) gained rally-bred upgrades including a more powerful engine, a firmer suspension, and a more muscular-looking design characterized by a functional hood scoop and a rear spoiler. Power comes from a 2.0-liter turbocharged flat 4 engine, rated at 227 horsepower and 217 lb-ft. Output is sent to all 4 wheels through a 5-speed manual transmission.
